letter.purpose: Carol's letter on the first screen (--text-letter), wrapped like a paragraph, about 34 characters wide.

headline.purpose: Section headings (--text-heading), with one italic key phrase.

title.purpose: How-it-works step titles and the recognition line (--text-xl).

body-large.purpose: Stage body text, invitation text, testimonial quotes, letter links (--text-lg).

label.purpose: Captions, testimonial names, placeholder labels, the footer (--text-sm). Never uppercase eyebrows.

motion.name: ease-out

motion.name: duration-slow

narrative.northStar: A short, signed letter from Carol
narrative.overview:
Chosen 2026-10-28: the fonts from "Warm editorial" with the colours from "Modern confident". The result should feel warm and experienced in its type, and clean and current in its colour. Think a thoughtful conversation, not a corporate brochure.

Home reads as a short, signed letter from Carol. The page is mostly white and charcoal, set in a serif at letter size. Colour comes in fields: lilac for quotes and the how-it-works band, deep violet for the close.
keyCharacteristics: White and charcoal, set in Newsreader at letter size
One violet italic phrase per heading
Lilac fields for quotes and the how-it-works band
Apricot only for the jump-target highlight
A deep violet close with an italic white signature
Pill buttons, underlined violet links, no shadows or gradients

rules.name: The Deep Violet Close
rules.body: The invitation that ends a page sits on a full-bleed --color-primary-dark band with white text and an italic white "Carol" signature. Its key phrase stays white and relies on the italic alone, because violet on violet would not read. Use the light button there, never the violet one.

rules.name: The Apricot Rule
rules.body: Apricot is reserved for one job: the highlight that draws under a stage heading when a visitor has jumped to it (:target). Never use it for text, backgrounds, buttons or decoration.

rules.name: The One Phrase Rule
rules.body: Each heading has one key phrase in italic. On white it is violet; on deep violet it stays white.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No eyebrow or kicker labels above headings. The heading says it on its own.

dos: Use violet sparingly: one main button per screen, and italic violet for the key phrase in a headline.
Be generous with spacing in steps of 8px: white space is part of the calm.
Lead with Carol's own black-and-white portraits.
donts: No drop shadows and no colour gradients.
Avoid generic stock metaphors (ladders, jumping dancers, handshakes).
No eyebrow or kicker labels above headings.
